metadata.note: The Bucksport and Bangor Railroad, Bangor - Brewer Junction - Bucksport, Maine: one physical line of 18.8-19.3 mi, never extended, later the Maine Central's Bucksport Branch. Drawn from research/branches/bucksport_and_bangor_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-10-10; only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4: three features share identical geometry, split by who ran the trains - European and North American Railway (lessee, Dec 1874 - 1 Oct 1879), the Bucksport and Bangor Railroad (worked by lessee L. L. Lincoln, then from 1882 by the same company reorganized as the Eastern Maine Railroad, to 1 May 1883 - the report's blocks [2] and [3] merged because a renamed company is one company), and the Maine Central (1883 - 27 Jan 1932). The 1932 end applies to Brewer Jct - Bucksport; Bangor - Brewer Jct kept the Bar Harbor / Calais trains and is drawn for those years in bar_harbor_express.geojson.

not_yet_sourced: Charter year: 1870, 1871 (Poor's 1880-85), 1872 (Poor's 1876) or 1873 (Peters 1976) - does not affect drawn years.
Eastern Maine reorganization date: 1 Feb 1882 (Poor's 1884) vs 1 Feb 1883 (Poor's 1885). Drawn inside the merged Bucksport and Bangor feature, so the split does not depend on it.
Name of the 1882 company: 'Eastern Maine Railroad' (Poor's) vs 'Eastern Maine Shoreline Railway' (Wikipedia/Peters 1976).
Gauge: 5 ft 6 in (Fowler) vs standard (Poor's 1876) at opening; 3 ft (Poor's) vs 3 ft 6 in (Fowler) for 1879-83; MEC standard-gauging 1883 (Poor's) vs 1884 (historic-structures.com).

Whether the 1879-83 narrow gauge reached Bangor or only Brewer Jct (Fowler queries it; Poor's says Bangor throughout). If a Brewer-terminus era is found, the Bucksport and Bangor feature needs a Brewer - Bucksport geometry.
Whether service was suspended during the 1879-80 regauging.
MEC lease date: 1 May 1883 (Poor's) vs 1884 (historic-structures.com, Wikipedia 'Bucksport station').
Bangor terminal 1874-1906 (before Union Station opened in 1907) - not established; only the last half-mile of geometry is affected.
Date of the Bangor - Brewer railroad bridge (1873 per an unverified Bangor Daily News snippet).
All headways and speeds: no timetable for any era was read; the 1880-81 figure is derived from Poor's train-miles.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Not drawn: Brewer Jct - Bucksport freight service 27 Jan 1932 - Dec 2014 (Bucksport paper mill, South Orrington chemical plant), and any wharf spur at Bucksport (Spofford's Wharf / 'Lower Station', not confirmed as passenger). MEC Table 12 Bangor-Bucksport (1940, 1952) is a motor-coach table and is not drawn.
metadata.horsecar_audit: None - steam from opening (first locomotive landed at Bucksport 17 Sep 1874).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 19.0 mi Bangor - Bucksport against a documented 18.80 mi (Poor's Manual 1876-1884) and 19.3 mi from Bangor Union Station (Fowler; MEC 1917 station handbook via Wikipedia). Brewer Jct - Bucksport (18.0 mi) is opstrace.py over OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=MEC, 100% on the live/dormant CSX 'Bucksport Branch' (plus its 0.09-mi abandoned stub to the Bucksport depot), against Fowler's MP 1.3 - 19.3 = 18.0 mi. Bangor - Brewer Jct (1.1 mi) is hand-assembled from OSM: the Waterville Subdivision from the Bangor station area north-east to the north end of the Penobscot River railroad bridge, the bridge (OSM way 43469586, 'Bucksport Branch') and the Brewer approach to Brewer Jct (44.79324 N, -68.76151), which lies 1.5 m from the Bar Harbor Express geometry in bar_harbor_express.geojson, so the junction meets. APPROXIMATED: one straight leg of 0.3 mi at Bangor, from the Union Station point used by bar_harbor_express.geojson (-68.7712, 44.8016) to the Kenduskeag bridge on the Waterville Subdivision, copied from that layer so both terminals coincide. SIMPLIFIED: Fowler marks a '0.5 Junction (reverse ?)' - trains appear to have run north-east past the bridge to the wye and backed onto it; that out-and-back is not drawn, and the line steps directly from the Waterville Subdivision onto the bridge through a ~15 m connector at its north end, which is why the trace is a little under Fowler's 19.3. ERA CAVEAT: the Bangor terminal drawn is the 1907 Union Station site; the 1874-1906 Bangor station is not established (report UNRESOLVED 6) and is not drawn separately. All eras are drawn on the alignment as it survives today (standard-gauge MEC/CSX track); any differences in the 1874 broad/standard or 1879-83 narrow-gauge alignment are unmapped. Simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 8 m.

segments.note: The Bucksport and Bangor Railroad's line, leased on opening to the European and North American Railway at 40% of gross (35% from Nov 1876), which worked it as a branch of its Bangor - Vanceboro line with its own rolling stock. Built as Bangor's winter outlet to open water at Bucksport. Opening day is disputed, the year is not: first train into Bangor Sat 28 Nov 1874 (Worcester Daily Spy, 1 Dec 1874); 'opened' 12 Dec 1874 (Poor's 1880-1885); regular trains over the whole length 21 Dec 1874 (Wikipedia citing Peters 1976). The E&NA's Oct 1876 surrender to its mortgage trustees and the B&B's own March 1879 foreclosure sale to its bondholders did not change who ran the trains. The E&NA lease expired 1 Oct 1879 (Poor's 1880). Gauge at opening is a source conflict: 5 ft 6 in (Fowler) vs 4 ft 8 1/2 in (Poor's 1876); both agree it was standard by 1877. Headway 720 (about two trains a day) is an ESTIMATE - no timetable for this era was read; Poor's 1876 gives only gross earnings (~$20,000 for 1875). Speed is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Poor's 1876-77 and 1880 editions for the 1874 opening, the E&NA lease and its 1 Oct 1879 expiry; Worcester Daily Spy 1 Dec 1874 for the first train; Fowler line 13 (1876 Pathfinder letter y) for public stops by 1876. Headway and speed NOT SOURCED (estimates).

segments.note: Worked by the Bucksport and Bangor's own interests from the end of the E&NA lease (1 Oct 1879): first by L. L. Lincoln, 'Lessee, Superintendent and Treasurer', under a ten-year lease at 33 1/3% of gross (Poor's 1880, 1881), with the road's own narrow-gauge stock (2 locomotives, 2-3 passenger cars). The line was narrowed from standard gauge 'during the past year' (Poor's 1881) - 3 ft per Poor's, 3 ft 6 in per Fowler (conflict); whether trains ran straight through the regauging in late 1879 / 1880 is not known, so a short suspension inside this span is possible. Fowler queries whether the narrow gauge ran only 'from Brewer Jn?'; Poor's describes Bangor - Bucksport, 18.80 mi, throughout, so the full line is drawn. The bondholders then reorganized the same company as the EASTERN MAINE RAILROAD and operated it directly, Lincoln remaining superintendent - one company renamed, so one feature here (CLAUDE.md Rule 4). The rename date is a SOURCE CONFLICT: 1 Feb 1882 (Poor's 1884; Poor's 1882 already reports it done) vs 1 Feb 1883 (Poor's 1885). Wikipedia's 'Eastern Maine Shoreline Railway' (from Peters 1976) is a name Poor's never uses. Ends 1 May 1883 with the perpetual lease to the Maine Central (Poor's 1884, 1885). An extension to Ellsworth was proposed in this era and never built. Headway 360 is DERIVED, not printed: 21,645 and 32,240 passenger train-miles in the years to 30 Sep 1880 and 1881 on 18.8 mi is about 2 then 3 round trips a day; treat it as an estimate. Speed is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Poor's 1880, 1881 and 1882 editions (Bucksport and Bangor entries) for the Lincoln lease, the 3 ft regauging and the train-mile figures the headway is derived from; Poor's 1882, 1884 and 1885 editions for the Eastern Maine reorganization (1882 vs 1883 conflict) and the 1 May 1883 MEC lease. Headway DERIVED, speed NOT SOURCED (estimates).

segments.note: Maine Central Bucksport Branch, leased in perpetuity from 1 May 1883 at $9,500 a year (Poor's 1884, 1885); historic-structures.com and Wikipedia's 'Bucksport station' give 1884 for the MEC takeover - conflict, Poor's preferred as contemporary. The MEC changed the gauge back to standard on taking the lease (Poor's 1884). From 1884 the Mount Desert Branch (and later the Calais trains) left this line at Brewer Junction, MP 1.3, so the Bangor - Brewer Jct leg kept passenger trains after 1932 - those are drawn in bar_harbor_express.geojson, not here. The last passenger train from Bangor to Bucksport ran 27 Jan 1932 (Johnson 1985 p.111, via Wikipedia), consistent with Fowler's letter c (1932 MEC timetable) and no letter d (1954). The MEC replaced the trains with its own buses: MEC Table 12 Bangor-Bucksport in the 1 Jan 1940 timetable and the Feb 1952 Official Guide is a BUS table, not rail. Freight to the Bucksport paper mill and the South Orrington chemical plant continued until December 2014 - context only; that is not passenger service and is not drawn. Headway 360 (about two trains each way a day) is an ESTIMATE carried over from the 1880-81 train-mile figures; no MEC branch timetable was read. Speed is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Poor's 1884 and 1885 editions for the 1 May 1883 MEC lease; Wikipedia 'Bucksport Branch' citing Johnson 1985 p.111 for the 27 Jan 1932 last passenger train; Fowler line 13 letters y-c. Headway and speed NOT SOURCED (estimates).
